task_summary: Analyze lake water temperature for long-term warming trends and identify the most important driving factor category (Heat/Flow/Wind/Human) from climate, hydrology, and land cover data.
decomposition_rationale: The task has two distinct analytical phases: (1) trend detection using Mann-Kendall statistics, and (2) driving factor attribution using ML-based feature importance with category aggregation. A data loading/merging skill is foundational to both. Three skills cleanly separate data pipeline, trend analysis, and factor attribution concerns.

skills.name: evo-lake-data-pipeline
skills.description: Loads, merges, and preprocesses the four CSV datasets (water_temperature, climate, land_cover, hydrology) into analysis-ready DataFrames. Handles date parsing, temporal alignment, annual aggregation, and NaN management.
skills.responsibility: All data I/O, merging, resampling, and cleaning. Produces unified DataFrames ready for trend analysis and factor attribution.

skills.name: evo-lake-trend-analysis
skills.description: Performs non-parametric Mann-Kendall trend detection on lake water temperature time series using pymannkendall, outputting slope and p-value to trend_result.csv.
skills.responsibility: Trend detection on water temperature series, handling autocorrelation via modified MK tests, NaN removal, and CSV output of slope and p-value.

skills.name: evo-lake-factor-attribution
skills.description: Trains a Random Forest model to determine feature importances of environmental predictors, maps features to categories (Heat/Flow/Wind/Human), sums contributions per category, and outputs the dominant factor to dominant_factor.csv.
skills.responsibility: ML-based feature importance extraction, manual category mapping of all predictor variables, aggregation of importance by category, identification of the single most important category, and CSV output.
